Hundreds of Mozambicans Flee to Malawi to Escape Fighting 
chttp://hosted.ap.org/dynamicistories/A/AF_MOZAMBIQUE_H UN DREDS_F LEE?SITE=AP&SECTION =HOM E&TEM PLATE= 
DEFAULT&CTIME=2015-07-27-10-44-17> 
July 2015 
MAPUTO (AP) - A Malawian official says hundreds of Mozambicans have fled into the neighboring country 
following fighting between the government and opposition fighters. 
EFTA_R1_01377401 
EFTA02372882
--- PAGE 2 ---
Commissioner for Malawi's Mwanza district, Gift Rapozo, told The Associated Press Monday that about 700 
Mozambicans fled into the country two weeks ago and more are crossing the border to escape fighting between the 
Mozambican army and fighters loyal to the opposition party Renamo. 
Mozambican Agriculture Minister Jose Pacheco, who is the government's chief negotiator with Renamo, said 
Renamo fighters carried out two attacks in northern Tete province, violating a peace agreement signed last year before 
the general elections. 
Renamo's chief negotiator, Simon Macuiane said the government must provide proof of the attacks. 
Renamo and Frelimo signed a peace accord in September last year.
